label: S. 4835
title: Bureau of Industry and Security License Administration Enhancement Act

items.item: Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS)
items.snippet: This bill revises certain processes used by the Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) to review applications for export licenses.
(An is informed letter notifies individual companies and universities of supplemental license requirements and requires compliance with the letter's license requirements.
BIS guidance states that noncompliance with a letter is treated the same as noncompliance with any other license requirement…

…with a letter is treated the same as noncompliance with any other license requirement under the Export Administration Regulations.) The bill requires any is informed letter or similar guidance or communication to be terminated within 60…
BIS must submit these factors to Congress prior to publishing them in the Federal Register.

lobbying.caption: From Senate lobbying disclosures (LD-2). A filing mentions this bill; it does not show what was asked for, which side the client took, or any contact with this member. Reported amounts cover the whole filing, not this bill alone.
lobbying.amount_note: Amounts are the income or expenses reported on the whole LD-2 filing, not money spent on this bill.

caption: This shows who the bill names and who lobbied on it. It does not show who gains or loses, and lobbying can be for or against a bill.

C001096.label: Overlap, not proof of influence.
C001096.caption: Money from this member's itemized individual donors (over $200) whose self-reported employer falls in an industry that also has a client lobbying on this bill. Correlation only; not a quid pro quo. Donors give to campaigns for many reasons, and a lobbying client may have opposed the bill.
C001096.note: None of the lobbying clients on this bill matched an industry rule, so there is nothing to compare.
